analysis: The PR changes documentation only: docs/developer/build.md (new paragraph near line 37, with an unrelated head excerpt at lines 500-569) and docs/developer/test.md (new 'Provider authorization guidance' section at head lines 76-87). No executable code, configuration, keys, endpoints, or trust-boundary behavior changes. The new test.md section describes running ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests, which exercise freshness checks and summaries used by status and doctor: an unexpired late serving lease stays visible, and removal advice needs a matching fresh decision. This relates to TB-011, T-053, T-057 and A-016. The text states that the tests use fixed snapshots and injected process identity, do not run host probes or native Apple operations, and do not establish App Attest acceptance. That is an appropriately scoped evidence limit and does not overclaim qualification (T-056/T-054). The build.md text is the same. I found no new attack surface, no weakened assumption, and no security-control change. The base-text excerpts of test.md (lines 1-920) and the build.md head excerpt (lines 500-569) are unchanged context, and I saw nothing in them that this PR newly invalidates. One integration point remains outside the supplied evidence. The test-suite and production code behind 'late but unexpired lease stays visible while removal advice requires fresh decision' are not in this batch. A reviewer of the code PR should check that status and doctor advice never treats a stale decision as authorization or as grounds to remove MDM, which is relevant to T-057 and T-052. No documentation-only issue qualifies as a finding.
